**Subject: CalVIP Grant Application – Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC)**

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC), a minority-owned social enterprise, requests $500,000 from CalVIP to significantly expand our gun safety education and violence prevention initiatives in Sacramento’s communities of color. Our mission directly addresses the critical need for culturally competent, community-led solutions to reduce gun violence and accidental shootings that disproportionately impact our neighborhoods. This crisis demands innovative and trustworthy interventions.

Our multi-pronged program uniquely engages the community. Our flagship "Gloxsie 21" cartoon IP connects with youth through age-appropriate narratives on safe gun practices and conflict resolution. We then leverage this engagement with our AI education component, empowering residents with critical thinking and digital literacy skills essential for discerning information and making informed safety choices in a complex world. Complementing these, hands-on community workshops, hosted by our partner Church of Legacy, provide vital training in safe storage, de-escalation techniques, and understanding gun laws.

With CalVIP support, we anticipate a measurable reduction in accidental shootings and gun-related incidents, alongside increased community knowledge of safe gun practices. Outcomes will include improved safe storage compliance, heightened awareness of de-escalation strategies, and a stronger culture of responsible gun ownership. We will track workshop attendance, pre/post knowledge assessments, and community survey data to demonstrate impact.

GAFC is uniquely qualified as a minority-owned enterprise with deep, authentic roots in the communities we serve. Our innovative approach, combining youth-focused IP, cutting-edge AI education, and direct community engagement via a trusted partner like Church of Legacy, ensures accessibility and relevance. We understand the nuances of addressing violence within our community and are committed to empowering residents with the knowledge and skills for a safer future.
